title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 open: God wills the saving grace of the Gospel offered promiscuously to all — Mat. 28:19; Mk 16:15; Col. 1:28
pass_a_gloss: God wills that the saving grace of the Gospel be offered promiscuously unto all men: which his will he has opened in many places of Scripture, Matt. xxviii. 19, Go ye therefore and teach all nations, etc. And Mark xvi. 15. Go ye into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. Hence also the Apostle Col. i. 28. We announce Christ, warning every man, and teaching every man, that we may present every man perfect in Christ. This affection of God toward the salvation of all men seems to argue that no one was reprobated by him, except after consideration of grace contemned, or (which comes to the same) except from foresight of final unbelief and impenitence.
pass_b_english: God wills that the saving grace of the Gospel be offered to all men alike — a will he has opened in many Scriptures: Matt. 28:19, Go therefore and teach all nations; and Mark 16:15, Go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. So also the Apostle, Col. 1:28: We announce Christ, warning every man and teaching every man, that we may present every man perfect in Christ. This regard of God for all men's salvation seems to argue that he reprobated no one except after regard to contempt of grace — or, what comes to the same, except from foresight of final unbelief and impenitence.
source_text: Deus vult ut salutaris gratia Evangelii omnibus hominibus promiscue offeratur: quam suam voluntatem multis Scripturae locis patefecit, Matth. xxviii. 19, Euntes ergo docete omnes gentes, etc. Et Marc. xvi. 15. Euntes in mundum universum praedicate Evangelium omni creaturae. Hinc etiam Apostolus Coloss. i. 28. Nos annunciamus Christum, corripientes omnem hominem, et docentes omnem hominem, ut exhibeamus omnem hominem perfectum in Christo. Hic affectus Dei erga omnium hominum salutem, videtur arguere neminem ab eo fuisse reprobatum, nisi post considerationem gratiae contemtae, vel (quod eodem redit) nisi ex praevisione finalis infidelitatis et impoenitentiae.
